status: frozen before fitting after the committed pre-fit inventory
estimand: Incremental predictive association of first re-election after a first-ever electorate win with the later normalized candidate residual, conditional on an earlier residual and known recontesting candidacy. It is not a causal freshman or uniquely personal-vote effect.
unit: One Stage 8 linked source-winner to next-election candidacy pair, with percentage-point residuals; one pair contributes one equal weight.
primaryScope: General electorates only; observed held matched contests with both normalized residuals; same electorate and unchanged published boundary regime in 2008→2011, 2014→2017 or 2020→2023. Māori remains separate and cannot yield a coefficient with zero classified source-winner pairs.
treatment: First-ever dated electorate service begins on the source general-election date, source candidate won, and service continues through target-election day. No earlier electorate interval, no prior list service in primary, no interrupted service. Target candidacy is known independently of target victory.
comparator: Source-winning recontester with reconciled earlier continuous electorate service, excluding seat switches at source, returning/former electorate careers, off-cycle entries, interrupted service, unresolved identity or career history. Prior list service among experienced incumbents is retained and disclosed because it does not redefine electorate tenure.
identityAndMissingness: A unique official profile surname and source-seat/date service row corroborates the source winner; profile career start must reconcile with its dated service table. Stage 8 target identity can be probable on an exact chain, recorded and restricted to confirmed in sensitivity. Unmatched, ambiguous or incomplete tenure stays unknown. All exclusions are recorded. Retrospective publication/retrieval timing is distinct from historical service dates.

equations.changeSensitivity: mean(y_i - x_i | T_i=1) - mean(y_i - x_i | T_i=0)
equations.units: x and y are additive normalized residuals in percentage points; gamma is a percentage-point incremental association. Ordinary least squares with equal pair weights and an intercept. Beta is jointly fitted only inside this Stage 9 diagnostic; Stage 8 operational persistence remains null.

interceptRationale: The later residual need not be zero when the earlier residual is zero because party/election references and selection can shift between elections. Stage 6's zero-intercept elasticity assumption addresses a different estimand and is not inherited.
approachComparison: A freshman mean residual omits baseline. A group difference in before/after change implicitly fixes persistence to one and is vulnerable to regression to the mean if source residual distributions differ. The joint common-slope model adjusts the source residual and compares experienced incumbents with one additional indicator, with the change difference retained as sensitivity. This is a predictive adjustment, not identification of a causal effect.
validation: 2011 has no prior same-design training transition and is benchmark/descriptive only. For 2017, fit using 2011 targets only; for 2023, fit using 2011 and 2017 targets only. Each target evaluation uses models fitted on earlier target elections, the same eligible holdout pairs, and only source-election residual/status as predictors. Report MAE/RMSE in percentage points, treatment/comparator counts, fitted coefficients and both simple benchmarks. No target reference offset, target residual, target winner flag or later winner flag enters a predictor or cohort selection.
selectionCriteria: A non-null operational freshman effect requires identifiable treatment and comparator in both trained holdouts, a consistent fitted effect direction across folds/full sample, non-worse MAE and RMSE than the no-freshman model in each trained holdout, at least 0.25 percentage point pooled MAE improvement, no material reversal under proportional/log-odds and prior-list sensitivity, and adequate identity/geography breadth for the intended population. Failure of any criterion selects null; this does not change Stage 8 selection. Target-confirmed identity restriction is a winner-selected retrospective diagnostic and cannot support operational selection.
uncertainty: Report transition-level scores and effect variation rather than candidate-pair iid standard errors or significance. Only three source/target transition clusters, repeated people and shared party/election leave-one-out references limit uncertainty claims. A leave-one-transition-out descriptive effect stability check is permitted where both groups remain.
sensitivities: proportional and log-odds normalized residuals on their available identical paired samples
include first-term prior-list MPs as a separately labelled group
restrict both Stage 8 occurrence links to confirmed as a target-winner-selected retrospective diagnostic only
difference in mean changes by group
target-win/loss composition as retrospective diagnostic only
limitations: Conditional on recontesting and bounded profile availability, which select successful/prominent MPs. Retrospective profile publication may depend on later outcomes. First-win election may be unusually favourable; regression to the mean, stable seat/party context, national party changes, tenure length and retirement selection can mimic a freshman association. Same-name/seat geography is never used to override boundary restrictions. Do not add gamma as an independent Stage 6/7/8 bonus or transport residuals to changed 2026 boundaries.
outputs: inventory.json and tenure-evidence.json remain pinned pre-fit artifacts
analysis.json contains descriptive fits, chronological metrics, benchmarks and sensitivities
selection.json contains nullable selectedOperationalFreshmanEffectPP and explicit gates
analysis-manifest.json hashes the frozen inputs, analysis code and outputs
reproducibility: Offline Stage 9 analysis consumes the committed pre-fit inventory, Stage 8 pairs and this specification with stage-specific checksums. It does not rewrite Stage 5–8 artifacts or the shared source registry.
